questions.stem: A CI job must build only `state:modified` resources, but any `ref()` they make to unselected, unbuilt parent models must resolve to the production versions of those parents instead of failing. The team needs the exact command-line combination that achieves this against a `prod-artifacts` directory. Which combination is correct?

option_texts.A: `dbt build --select state:modified --defer --state path/to/prod-artifacts/`, so unselected nodes not yet built here resolve to production via deferral
option_texts.B: `dbt build --select state:modified --full-refresh`, since full-refresh also resolves any unselected missing upstream parents automatically
option_texts.C: `dbt build --select state:modified --exclude prod-artifacts`, so the build does not try to resolve unselected production objects at all
option_texts.D: `dbt clone --select state:modified --state path/to/prod-artifacts/`, which copies the production parents into the CI schema first

questions.drill_rationale: When deferral conditions are met, dbt will resolve ref calls using the state manifest instead, but only if the node isn't among the selected nodes, and it doesn't exist in the database.
questions.decision_hinge: When deferral conditions are met, dbt will resolve ref calls using the state manifest instead, but only if the node isn't among the selected nodes, and it doesn't exist in the database.

plausible_options.D: must resolve to the production versions of those parents instead of failing

eliminated_by.C: against a `prod-artifacts` directory

distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated — full-refresh rebuilds incremental models from scratch, it does not resolve missing upstream parents
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated — `--exclude` removes resources from selection, it is not a state or deferral mechanism
distractor_traps.D: T7: over-engineering — cloning copies objects into the schema; deferral achieves the same ref resolution without copying anything

questions.stem: A CI run executes `dbt build --select state:modified+ --defer --state ./prod-manifest/`. Only `stg_orders` was modified; `fct_orders` refs `stg_orders` and is selected as a downstream descendant; `dim_customers` is an unrelated, unselected, already-built parent that `fct_orders` also refs. The team needs to know what happens to `dim_customers` during this run. What happens?

option_texts.A: dbt resolves the `ref()` to `dim_customers` using the production manifest, since it is not among the selected nodes and already exists there
option_texts.B: `dim_customers` is rebuilt anyway, because the trailing `+` after `state:modified` also selects all of its ancestors
option_texts.C: The build fails, because `dim_customers` was not explicitly selected and `--defer` cannot resolve unselected parents
option_texts.D: `dim_customers` is skipped entirely and `fct_orders` builds without any data from it

questions.drill_answer_short: An unselected parent that already exists in the database gets deferred to the production manifest
questions.drill_rationale: When deferral conditions are met, dbt will resolve ref calls using the state manifest instead, but only if the node isn't among the selected nodes, and it doesn't exist in the database (or --favor-state is used).
questions.decision_hinge: When deferral conditions are met, dbt will resolve ref calls using the state manifest instead, but only if the node isn't among the selected nodes, and it doesn't exist in the database (or --favor-state is used).

plausible_options.B: `fct_orders` refs `stg_orders` and is selected as a downstream descendant

C.signal: is an unrelated, unselected, already-built parent that `fct_orders` also refs
C.requires_fact: When deferral conditions are met, dbt resolves ref calls using the state manifest instead, when the node isn't among the selected nodes and it doesn't exist in the database.

eliminated_by.D: `fct_orders` refs `stg_orders` and is selected as a downstream descendant

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling — a trailing `+` selects descendants of the modified node, not ancestors of every node it references
distractor_traps.C: T4: breaks a stated fact — resolving an unselected, already-built parent via the state manifest is exactly what deferral does
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated — dbt does not silently drop an unselected parent's data

questions.stem: A pull request changes a model's `materialized` config from `view` to `table`, and separately adds a new `meta: {owner: data-team}` entry to an unrelated model, with no other changes anywhere. The reviewer needs to know which of these two changes `state:modified` actually detects by default. Which TWO statements are correct?

option_texts.A: The materialization change is detected, because any config change can affect how the model is built
option_texts.B: The `meta` change is NOT detected, because dbt treats `meta` as metadata only and it does not trigger `state:modified`
option_texts.C: The `meta` change is detected, because any property change in a YAML file counts as a modification
option_texts.D: Neither change is detected, because `state:modified` only tracks config changes made directly in raw `.sql` files

questions.decision_hinge: Changes to tags and meta, whether set at the resource level or on individual columns in a YAML file, don't count as modifications and will not trigger state:modified. Any other config change counts as a modification, because that config could affect materialization.

questions.drill_answer_short: A trailing + adds descendants of the matched nodes to the selection
questions.drill_rationale: Placed after a model/resource, the + operator includes the resource itself and all its descendants (downstream dependencies). Placed before, it includes ancestors (upstream dependencies) instead.
questions.decision_hinge: Placed after a model/resource, the + operator includes the resource itself and all its descendants (downstream dependencies). Placed before, it includes ancestors (upstream dependencies) instead.

distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling — a leading + adds ancestors; a trailing + adds descendants instead
distractor_traps.D: T4: breaks a stated fact — a trailing + does change the selection by adding descendants
